plan.outcomes:
After this lesson you can:
- predict whether a browser reuses its saved copy or asks the server
- choose a sensible Cache-Control max-age for a given file
plan.prerequisites:
- Know that a browser requests files from a server over HTTP
- No prior knowledge of caching
plan.teachingPrinciples:
- Start from a question learners can answer by intuition
- One new idea per slide
- Learners attempt before they see the answer
- Images are teaching diagrams, not decoration
plan.progression:
1. A nearby copy is faster than a trip to a far server.
2. A copy can go stale.
3. So something must decide how long to trust the copy (freshness).
4. When trust expires, ask cheaply (validation).

titleSlide.title: Why browsers keep copies
titleSlide.text: How a browser decides when its saved copy of a page is still good enough.

image.concept: A browser holding a stack of saved page copies, reaching past a far-away server to the nearest copy.

slides.title: Why is the second visit faster?
slides.text: You open a page, close it, and reopen it a minute later. Why does it appear much faster the second time?
slides.purpose: Hook: surface the question the lesson answers (before progression step 1).
slides.speakerNotes:
Key points:
Learner predicts from intuition; no jargon yet

slides.title: A nearby copy beats a faraway trip
slides.text:
- Fetching from a distant server takes time
- A saved copy lets the browser skip the trip
- A copy can go out of date
- So something must decide how long to trust it

image.concept: Browser, a small box labelled "saved copy" beside it, and a far-away server; a short arrow vs a long arrow.

slides.speakerNotes:
Key points:
Copies are fast; copies go stale

slides.title: Trusting a copy for one hour
slides.text: With max-age=3600 the browser reuses its copy for one hour without asking.

image.concept: Timeline from 0 s to 3600 s labelled "reuse copy", then "must check".

slides.purpose: Progression step 3: freshness decides how long to trust.
slides.speakerNotes:
Key points:
max-age sets a freshness window

Pause and ask learners what they expect at second 3601.

slides.title: Asking cheaply when the copy expires
slides.text: If the file is unchanged, a tiny 304 reply replaces a full download.

image.concept: Request carrying an ETag; two replies: a tiny 304 or a full 200.

slides.purpose: Progression step 4: validation makes expiry cheap.
slides.speakerNotes:
Key points:
Validation is cheaper than a full download

slides.title: Your turn: pick a setting
slides.text:
- A site logo changes about once a year
- Its news feed changes every minute
- Choose a max-age for each and write why
- Answer before moving on

image.concept: Two file icons (logo, news feed) with empty boxes for max-age.

slides.purpose: Learner applies steps 2 to 4 before seeing an answer.
slides.speakerNotes:
Key points:
Apply staleness cost to a real choice

slides.title: Compare with a reasoned answer

image.concept: Logo and news-feed icons with the same max-age of one day.

afterImage.concept: Logo with max-age one year; news feed with validate on every visit.

slides.beforeCaption: Before: one setting for everything, so the feed goes stale.
slides.afterCaption: After: trust time matches how fast each file changes.
slides.purpose: Closes the loop on practice; ties back to staleness (step 2).
slides.speakerNotes:
Key points:
Match trust time to change rate

slides.title: Same idea elsewhere
slides.text:
- Copies are fast; copies go stale
- Freshness sets how long to trust
- Validation makes expiry cheap
- Offline phone maps and a pantry make the same trade-off

image.concept: Four-step chain recap plus two small examples (phone map, pantry).

slides.purpose: Consolidates the progression and transfers it.
slides.speakerNotes:
Key points:
Four-step chain; same trade-off elsewhere
